title: Universal Driver's License Required?
summary: Long statutory-construction essay arguing that driver's licenses, registration and titles reach only commercial use, so private travellers need none.

assertions.quote: the state is constitutionally barred from converting that right into a licensed article of commerce
The man or woman traveling privately, in a personal conveyance, with no commercial nexus, is not within the scope of that framework.
the natural person in this list is the natural person acting in a commercial capacity

verdicts.note: Definitions that list natural persons alongside firms include every individual; no court reads them as limited to commercial actors.
IRC 7701(a)(1) defines 'person' to include an individual as well as trusts, estates, partnerships and corporations; arguments that an individual is not a 'person' are uniformly rejected.

The Detaxer reading that the Income Tax Act definition of person (including corporations) excludes flesh-and-blood people is a legally incorrect proposition rejected in R v Lindsay (Canadian statute).
Arguments that humans are not 'persons' in law, or that law reaches only commercial or government actors, were implicitly rejected; in modern law every human is a legal person.

assertions.quote: They are commercial documents for commercial contrivances operated by commercial persons.

verdicts.note: Registration and titling statutes cover all vehicles on public roads and are enforced against private owners.
A private citizen driving his own car was validly convicted for lacking registration; states may require registration of 'all motor vehicles - those moving in interstate commerce as well as others'.

assertions.quote: almost every state in the union explicitly declares that the common law is the supreme rule of decision

verdicts.note: Reception statutes adopt English common law only where not inconsistent with state statutes, so statutes prevail.

assertions.quote: The commercial nexus at the federal level is therefore the commercial nexus at the state level

verdicts.note: 18 USC 31 defines terms only for that federal criminal chapter; state licensing laws use their own definitions.
Absent national legislation a state may set its own rules for all motor vehicles on its highways; state licensing rests on state police power, not on a federal commercial definition.
